findings.problem: The 'Samuel the prophet of Israel' explanation compares the baker's pick to grabbing the sprinkle jar and ends 'Good jar. Wrong cookie.' Because the comparison stands for the baker's answer, this calls the baker's answer wrong.

rule.text: Never says "wrong," "fail" or "bad" about a baker's answer.

findings.problem: The 'Scoffers' explanation goes through Acts 13:41, then says 'And Paul's last word to his listeners? Watch out that this doesn't happen to you (Acts 13:40).' In the text the warning (13:40) comes before the quote, and the quote from the prophets (13:41) is the actual end of the sermon. So it calls 13:40 his last word when the text shows it isn't.

rule.text: He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The 'encouragement' explanation says 'They read from the Law and the Prophets, then they open the floor to the visitors,' so the synagogue leaders are the ones reading. Acts 13:15 only says 'After the reading from the Law and the Prophets' and never says who read.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open. Who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The 'False' explanation says 'And after all that, God still gives His people the land as an inheritance (Acts 13:19).' The word 'still' ties the land gift to the forty years of conduct as if it came in spite of it. Acts 13:18-19 just puts the two side by side and doesn't connect them.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open. Who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The 'Ephesus' explanation sums up Acts 13:51 as 'Shake, stomp, walk.' The text says they shook the dust off their feet and went. It has no stomping.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The 'Down to Joppa' explanation says 'Paul is going to mention a different John later' (Acts 13:24-25) with no reference. It also puts '(Acts 13:13)' after 'the others keep traveling without him,' but their travel inland is in Acts 13:14.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The 'encouragement' explanation ends 'Paul is about to take it' with no reference. Paul stands up in Acts 13:16. The 'prophecy' explanation on the same card does cite (Acts 13:16) for the same fact.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The 'Saul son of Kish from Benjamin' explanation ends 'I know a thing or two about getting slid to the back of the drawer and staying there.' In his backstory he didn't stay there. The angels opened the drawer and called him. 'Staying there' changes his story.

rule.text: He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: Most right-answer explanations open the same way, by repeating the answer plus 'friend' and an exclamation: 'Encouragement, friend!', 'A king, friend.', 'David, friend!', 'Jesus, friend!', 'Moses, friend!', 'Grace, friend!', 'Jealousy, friend.', 'Driven out, friend.', 'Sandals!', 'Iconium!', 'The Gentiles!', 'The ends of the earth!', 'Scoffers it is.', 'Jerusalem it is.' Many missed-answer explanations also open with the same 'No X here' / 'X's not ...' pattern: 'No construction project here.', 'No idols in this warning.', 'No house keys being handed out here', 'No jail cell in this one.', 'No hesitating here', 'Joppa's not where this road goes', 'Jerusalem's not on the itinerary.', 'Corinth's not the stop.' Read in a row, they sound like a template.

rule.text: There is no formula. Each explanation sounds natural and different from the others.

findings.problem: Several explanations open with a short verdict that works like a reaction: 'That's right!' (1/4 True), 'True!' (2/2 True), 'False is right.' (2/10 False), 'False!' (2/12 False, 3/13 False), 'You got it, friend.' (3/2), 'Yes, friend!' (2/14), 'Nope, no warning.' (1/6). The code already shows a reaction ('Baked just right', 'Underbaked', and so on) before each explanation, so the baker gets a verdict twice. answer-explanations.md says the explanation never includes a reaction, but it only lists the code's phrases, so it isn't clear whether verdict openers like these count.
findings.question: Does 'The explanation never includes a reaction' also ban verdict openers like 'That's right!', 'True!', 'False is right.' and 'You got it', or only the listed reaction phrases?
